traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified: - Optional warning: The prefer-implements-annotation rule detects legacy @story + @req comments and reports a preferImplements message when enabled. The rule is a suggestion type and is disabled by default (not present in recommended/strict configs), so teams can opt in via ESLint severity. - Auto-fix support: For simple single-story blocks, the rule provides a fix that converts @story + @req lines into a single @supports line. Tests verify the exact transformed output. - Single story conversion: Tests cover conversion of a single @story with a single @req and with multiple @req lines into a single @supports line listing all requirement IDs, in order, on one line. - Multi-story detection: The implementation and tests verify two non-fixable categories: comments mixing @story/@req with @supports (cannotAutoFix) and comments with multiple @story paths in the same block (multiStoryDetected). Both produce diagnostics without a fix. - Preserve order and formatting: The fix logic reuses the original prefix and replaces only the story and req lines, leaving description and param tags in place. Tests compare full comment strings before and after fix, ensuring structure is preserved. - Configurable enforcement: The rule has no custom options; enforcement is controlled entirely by ESLint severities off, warn, and error. It is not included in plugin presets, and tests explicitly confirm this, matching the story’s requirement that default is off and severity is configurable. - Both formats valid: Tests confirm that comments with only @story, only @req, or only @supports are ignored by this rule, while the existing validation rules (valid-annotation-format, require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, valid-req-reference) continue to validate them independently. When the migration rule is disabled (default), legacy annotations remain fully valid. - Quality standards and valid output: The auto-fix only runs when patterns are simple, and it bails out for complex or ambiguous cases (extra tokens on @story/@req, multi-story, mixed supports). Combined with the existing validation tests for supports, this ensures that fixes produce valid annotations. - Documentation: The internal rule doc and the user-facing migration guide document auto-fix behavior, examples, limitations, and opt-in configuration. Together with passing Jest tests, this satisfies the story’s definition of done.
Given the concrete implementation, comprehensive tests tied to this story, and passing test suite, the story is fully implemented and in a passing state.
